action: Cloud, data-centre and AI providers with overseas customers: have export-control counsel read the BIS interim final rule and check how remote access to advanced AI compute by foreign end users is identified and controlled.
exec: New know-your-customer duties for overseas data centres could affect cloud and AI providers' international contracts.
org: Bureau of Industry and Security (US Commerce Department)
plain: A new US policy requires overseas data centres that serve companies in China, Russia, Iran and Cuba to identify who their end users are, aiming to stop indirect access to American AI technology.

key_findings: BIS released an interim final rule on remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, which its announcement calls super intelligence technology.
The aim is to stop existing export restrictions being sidestepped through remote computing arrangements with data centres in third countries.
BIS says remote-access protections are being aligned with the controls already applied to physical shipments of sensitive technology.
The announcement names no countries, effective date or comment period; those details sit in the rule text, which was not read.
report.publisher: Bureau of Industry and Security (US Department of Commerce)
recommendations: Read the interim final rule linked from the BIS announcement for the actual obligations.
Use www.bis.gov for further information; the announcement itself lists no compliance steps.

sources.name: BIS news updates (announcement of the interim final rule)

summary: The Bureau of Industry and Security released an interim final rule on remote access to advanced AI chips and servers, aiming to stop export restrictions being sidestepped through data centers in third countries. Under the new policy, overseas data centers that serve firms in China, Russia, Iran and Cuba must identify their end users, according to SecurityWeek. The announcement itself names no countries, effective date or comment period.
title: US moves to block China's indirect access to American AI through overseas data centers

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Bureau of Industry and Security document (announcement only; the rule text was not loaded, so the country list and end-user duty rest on SecurityWeek).
